self|grant_writing_request: User requested a grants aim page on molecular subtypes and endometrial cancer
assistant|grant_aim_statement: Aim: To identify and characterize molecular subtypes of endometrial cancer and investigate their clinical and biological significance
assistant|endometrial_cancer_epidemiolog: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecological malignancy in developed countries with increasing worldwide incidence
assistant|endometrial_cancer_survival: Survival rate for advanced stages of endometrial cancer remains poor despite advances in surgical and radiation therapy
assistant|grant_objective_1: Identify molecular subtypes of endometrial cancer using combined genomic and transcriptomic approaches
assistant|grant_objective_2: Investigate clinical and biological significance of subtypes including association with patient outcomes and therapy response
assistant|grant_objective_3: Develop biomarkers for early detection and prognosis of endometrial cancer based on identified subtypes
assistant|grant_methods: Comprehensive genomic and transcriptomic analysis via next-generation sequencing plus unsupervised and supervised machine learning to identify subtypes
assistant|grant_validation_plan: Validate identified subtypes using an independent cohort of endometrial cancer samples with functional and bioinformatic approaches
assistant|grant_expected_outcomes: Expected: novel molecular subtypes identified, biomarkers developed, improved patient outcomes
assistant|grant_impact: Research will provide insights into molecular mechanisms and pave the way for new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies
